casos.causa: dir_file_sink.accept() joined attacker-controlled ZIP member names verbatim with os.path.join (which discards the base for absolute paths) and created parent dirs on the traversed path, allowing '../' and absolute-path members to write outside the output directory (CWE-22 zip-slip).

diff --git a/keynote_parser/file_utils.py b/keynote_parser/file_utils.py
index dfdafd1..01c71b0 100644
--- a/keynote_parser/file_utils.py
+++ b/keynote_parser/file_utils.py
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@

+import ntpath
 import os
 import sys
 
@@ -73,6 +74,33 @@ def to_yaml_data(contents):
     return contents.to_dict() if isinstance(contents, IWAFile) else contents
 
 
+def safe_target_path(target_dir, filename):
+    """Resolve an archive member name to a path confined inside target_dir.
+
+    Strips drive letters, leading separators and parent-directory (..)
+    components (which os.path.join would otherwise let escape the target,
+    since joining with an absolute path discards the base), then confines
+    the resolved path to target_dir, following symlinks. Returns None for
+    names with no usable path left or that would still resolve outside
+    target_dir (zip-slip, CWE-22); callers should skip such members.
+    """
+    normalized = filename.replace("\\", "/")
+    normalized = ntpath.splitdrive(normalized)[1]
+    parts = [
+        part
+        for part in normalized.split("/")
+        if part not in ("", ".", "..") and ":" not in part
+    ]
+    if not parts:
+        return None
+    target_path = os.path.join(target_dir, *parts)
+    base = os.path.realpath(target_dir)
+    resolved = os.path.realpath(target_path)
+    if resolved != base and not resolved.startswith(base + os.sep):
+        return None
+    return resolved
+
+

-        target_path = os.path.join(target_dir, filename)

+        )

casos.causa: unstream_dir() joined unsanitized zip member names onto target_directory and passed them to archive.extract()/os.utime()/os.chmod(), and recreated symlinks with unvalidated targets, so a crafted zip could write files and chmod/utime files outside target_directory, including writes through an in-target symlink pointing outside (CWE-22/CWE-59).

index 0c004c8..c6ecf8e 100644
--- a/src/ansible_runner/utils/streaming.py
+++ b/src/ansible_runner/utils/streaming.py
@@ -60,6 +60,43 @@ def stream_dir(source_directory: str, stream: io.FileIO) -> None:
                     encoded_target.write(line)
 
 
+def _is_within_directory(base_directory: str, path: str) -> bool:
+    """Return True if ``path`` is ``base_directory`` or something inside it."""
+    base = os.path.abspath(base_directory)
+    candidate = os.path.abspath(path)
+    return candidate == base or candidate.startswith(base + os.sep)
+
+
+def _is_safe_archive_name(filename: str) -> bool:
+    """Return True if a zip member name cannot escape the target directory.
+
+    Blocks absolute paths (POSIX and Windows drive forms) and any ``..``
+    component. Note this must run on the raw name: a name like ``a/../b``
+    normalizes to something inside the target, but ``ZipFile.extract()``
+    sanitizes it differently (by dropping the ``..`` part), so the member
+    is unsafe whenever ``..`` appears at all.
+    """
+    if not filename:
+        return False
+    if os.path.isabs(filename):
+        return False
+    # Zip member names use "/" regardless of platform; also treat "\" as a
+    # separator here so Windows-style "..\\" traversal is caught anywhere.
+    if ".." in filename.replace("\\", "/").split("/"):
+        return False
+    normalized = os.path.normpath(filename)
+    if os.path.isabs(normalized):
+        return False
+    if normalized == os.pardir or normalized.startswith(os.pardir + os.sep):
+        return False
+    # Windows drive-letter absolute paths, not caught by os.path.isabs on POSIX
+    if len(normalized) > 1 and normalized[1] == ":":
+        return False
+    if normalized in ("", os.curdir):
+        return False
+    return True
+
